newsitem.title: UGANDA: Christian rebels kill 10 in Uganda - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Christian rebels kill 10 in Uganda - newspaper.

text.p: Christian fundamentalist rebels killed 10 civilians in a raid on two northern Ugandan villages on Wednesday, in their latest attack in the region, the government-owned New Vision newspaper reported on Friday.
The rebels, who numbered about 50, hacked their victims to death with machetes, cutlasses, metal bars and hoes, it said.
The rebels also abducted 11 people and burnt down more than 50 houses in Koch Ongako and Bungatira, tiny villages outside Gulu town, 345 km (215 miles) north of the capital Kampala.

The dissidents, from the fanatical Lord's Resistance Army (LRA), returned on Thursday and ordered villagers to leave the area since they were about to launch a major offensive against the army, the newspaper said.
The deaths on Wednesday brought to 40 the number of people killed by the LRA since Saturday, New Vision said.
The Ugandan army has deployed heavily in the region to try to contain the nine-year-old rebellion that has paralysed the north of the East African country.
An estimated 15,000 troops patrol the area but the rebels, led by 30-year-old former religious teacher Joseph Kony, have so far eluded them.
